Most smart home lighting solutions rely on small bulbs and plug-in adapters, but as the market matures, we're starting to see recessed ceiling lights with built-in Matter support and direct compatibility with Apple Home. SwitchBot recently launched the new SwitchBot RGBICWW ceiling light, which natively supports Matter with no additional setup required and delivers impressively high brightness output.

HomeKit Weekly is a series dedicated to introducing smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Native Matter and Apple Home Integration

The biggest selling point of this new ceiling light is that it requires no SwitchBot Hub at all, offering out-of-the-box Matter support. As long as your Apple TV 4K or HomePod at home stays connected, the fixture can join your existing smart home system directly through the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.

Size and Brightness Specifications

SwitchBot offers two sizes to suit different scenarios: the 12-inch model is suitable for corridors and bathrooms, providing 2,000 lumens of brightness; the larger 15-inch model is ideal for living rooms and bedrooms, with a maximum brightness of up to 3,200 lumens. The product also supports stepless dimming, allowing smooth adjustment from 100% all the way down to 0%.

Standard smart bulbs can typically only display one color at a time, but this fixture uses RGBIC technology, which employs independent chips to simultaneously present multiple colors on the ceiling, creating rich and varied lighting effects. If you prefer more traditional lighting, it also comes equipped with dedicated warm white and cool white LEDs, with color temperature adjustable from 2700K to 6500K. Additionally, it features a power-off memory function—even during a brief power outage, the fixture will retain your previously set brightness and color. I really love this feature

Summary: SwitchBot RGBICWW

Using 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi means you'll need to keep an additional device running on the traditional band on your router. In my view, if it had a built-in Thread radio module supporting Mesh networking for near-instantaneous response times, the user experience would be even better. Being able to buy a wired-installed, natively Matter-supported ceiling light for under $50 is absolutely a highly cost-effective choice for anyone looking to permanently upgrade their ceiling lighting.

You can head to Amazon right now to buy this brand-new SwitchBot RGBICWW.
